probe: reproducible builds: why two builds of one commit differ
note: Read-only. Two scratch worktrees at paths differing by eight characters, built offline with the pinned toolchain and then removed; the main worktree was never modified and its binary is still 2d57ce864002406e. No build config, cargo setting or product code was changed: every option below was tested through the environment for the length of one build and left nowhere.

the_actual_cause.mechanism: cargo derives each package's -C metadata from its identity including its absolute path; rustc hashes that into the Cs<disambiguator>_ field of every v0-mangled symbol; the resulting name-length differences move unwind info, exception frames and constant layout

LC_UUID.note: content-derived by the linker: a consequence, not a cause

the_actual_cause.build_timestamp: none; the image carries LC_BUILD_VERSION, which is SDK and platform, not a clock

fixed_build_path.evidence: a clean rebuild of the same worktree returned 7d31698c9d839c97, byte-identical

remap_path_prefix.note: still differ, and both changed from their un-remapped values, so it is not a no-op

rustflags_c_metadata.note: cargo passes its own -C metadata after RUSTFLAGS, so cargo's wins

container_at_a_fixed_path.note: NOT MEASURED; no container was built

what_this_means_for_the_register: Every committed hash was produced at one path, ~/repos/minicon-surf/labs/native-dom, so the register is internally consistent and its hashes are re-derivable by anyone building the same commit at that same path. Measured earlier in this line of work, before the question was asked: ba46420b was rebuilt in the main worktree from a stashed source state and returned ba46420bb1e6d986, exactly the hash its receipt names. A register hash is a provenance token re-derivable at the same path, not a portable digest of the source.
